title: App Introduction Mechanism
description: Introduce a new "Introduction" mechanism: every app can declare a first-run walkthrough for first-time users. When started, a glass layer covers the whole screen; information boxes (less see-through than the glass) are placed per step; individual UI elements can be cut out of the glass (shown normally, interactive) or highlighted. Contract-first: IntroductionDefinition/IntroductionStepDefinition/IntroductionAnchor/IntroductionEmphasis/IntroductionPlacement/IntroductionAdvance in framework/core/rs/lib.rs, mirrored to TS. AppBuilder gets .introduction(...) with validation in build_definition(). Framework auto-injects a startIntroduction View action (replay via command palette) mirroring the setActiveTool precedent. React shell (framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx) owns runtime state (OverlayState.introductionStepIndex) and auto-starts on first launch per app (localStorage "seen" flag). New UIIntroduction component in ui/js/react/index.tsx renders a glass veil (new ui-glass-veil utility, more transparent than ui-glass-panel) with a live-tracked cutout rect (four bands, not SVG mask, so backdrop-filter glass survives and the hole is genuinely interactive), an optional pulsing highlight ring, and an info box using the panel glass tier. Steps support interactive advance: a step completes when the user activates a referenced tool or dispatches a referenced action, not just Next/Back/Skip buttons. wgpu/native renderer is out of scope (contract is renderer-agnostic, no schema change needed there). Proof-of-concept: give Puzzle 3D (puzzle3d-play app in puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs) a real introduction walkthrough covering its viewport, transform tools, and panels.
summary: Implemented the Introduction mechanism: a declarative, per-app first-run walkthrough. Contract (framework/core/rs/lib.rs): IntroductionDefinition/IntroductionStepDefinition/IntroductionAnchor/IntroductionEmphasis/IntroductionPlacement/IntroductionAdvance, AppDefinition.introduction, START_INTRODUCTION_ACTION_ID + start_introduction_action_definition() (mirrors setActiveTool). AppBuilder (framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs): .introduction() with full anchor/advance validation against declared window kinds/tools/actions/panel tabs, auto-injects startIntroduction. TS mirror regenerated and re-exported (framework/core/js/index.ts). CSS: --glass-veil-alpha/blur + ui-glass-veil utility (more transparent than the info-box's panel tier). React (ui/js/react/index.tsx): UIIntroduction renders a four-band glass veil around the live-tracked anchor rect (reuses existing ids/data-attributes for anchor resolution — zero markup changes needed elsewhere), an optional pulsing highlight ring, and an info box with Skip/Back/Next or an interactive-advance hint. An unresolved targeted anchor lets pointer events pass through the veil instead of trapping the user (found and fixed during live browser verification). Shell (framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx): OverlayState.introductionStepIndex, SET_INTRODUCTION_STEP reducer, startIntroduction interception + advance-on-action/advance-on-tool watching in onAction, auto-start effect keyed on a localStorage "seen" flag, mounted at the shell root. Puzzle 3D (puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs) got a real 5-step reference introduction (viewport highlight, interactive Move-tool step, catalogue panel tab, interactive add-object action step). Tests: 9 new Rust builder tests + 2 core serde round-trip tests (all passing, 146 total across the 3 touched Rust crates), 1 new reducer test, 3 new pure-function tests in ui-react (267 total, 14 pre-existing unrelated tree-rendering failures untouched). Verified live end-to-end in the puzzle-3d-react-dev browser: auto-start, Screen/WindowKind/Tool/Action anchors, Highlight ring, interactive advance on both tool activation and action dispatch, Skip persistence, and no re-trigger after being seen.
